title: Normalised transcript event
description: What the runner makes of one line of a Claude Code session transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl`), streamed to the hub on `GET /sessions/{id}/tail`. The mapping from the raw JSONL is SP2's table (scratch/spikes/SP2-worker-control/RESULT.md); `contracts/tests/reference_normalizer.py` is a reference implementation the runner may port. One JSONL line can give zero, one or several events (an assistant line with text and two tool calls gives three). The hub stores the ones the app shows as task events with the same `type` and `data` (app-api.yaml `TaskEvent`); it drops `thinking` and `turn_end`. A workflow's agents (SP10) are not in the main transcript: `workflow_start` there names the run, its `journal.jsonl` (`tail?workflow=`) gives `workflow_agent_start` and `workflow_agent_stop`, and each agent's own file is tailed with `workflow=` and `subagent=`. A pending permission is NOT here: it is not in the JSONL while the prompt is open; it comes from the runner's state stream (runner-api.yaml) and the channel.

offset.description: Byte offset just after the JSONL line this event came from (the same number as the SSE `id:`). Resume a tail from the last offset you processed; several events from one line share it.

index.description: Position of this event among those from the same line, starting at 0.

subagent_id.description: Set on every event of a subagent's own transcript (runner-api.yaml `tail?subagent=`); `offset` is then into that file.

workflow_id.description: Set on every event of a workflow's own stream (runner-api.yaml `tail?workflow=`, runner-api 0.1.12): the run's `journal.jsonl`, or with `subagent_id` too, one of its agents' transcripts. `offset` is then into that file.

source.description: For user text: where it came from when Claude Code says (`promptSource`), e.g. a channel message or a subagent hand-back.

examples.text: The bug is in `sub()`: it adds instead of subtracting. Fixing it now.

summary.description: One line for the collapsed row: the Bash command, the file path, the agent description, else the tool name.

input.description: The tool's input, truncated by the runner to 8 KB per string field.

denied.description: True when the user (or the relay) rejected the tool use (`toolDenialKind: user-rejected`).

text.description: The result as text, truncated to 8 KB.

Diff.description: From a tool result whose `toolUseResult` has a `structuredPatch` (Edit, Write, MultiEdit). Emitted after that tool's `tool_result`.

lines.description: Unified-diff lines, each starting with ' ', '+' or '-'.

agent_id.description: From the `Agent` call's launch result, which is where this event is emitted; absent only when that result did not name it.

description.description: The `Agent` call's own `description`, or `subagent` when it had none.

summary.description: The start of its hand-back report, truncated to 2 KB.

examples.summary: The buggy function is sub(): it returns a + b.

WorkflowStart.description: From the main transcript (runner-api 0.1.12): the `Workflow` tool's `tool_result` whose line's `toolUseResult` has `status: async_launched` and `taskType: local_workflow`. Emitted after that `tool_result`. `run_id` is what to tail with `workflow=` (SP10).

task_id.description: `toolUseResult.taskId`, Claude Code's background task id; absent when the line did not name it.

description.description: `toolUseResult.summary`: one line on what the workflow does.

examples.name: summarize-sp10-notes
examples.description: Read each of the 10 note files in sp10-files and return a one-line summary

WorkflowStop.description: From the main transcript: the later user line holding a `<task-notification>` whose `<tool-use-id>` is the `Workflow` call's. `status` is the notification's `<status>`; one the runner does not know is `unknown`.

run_id.description: The run, when the notification names it.

examples.summary: Dynamic workflow "Read each of the 10 note files in sp10-files and return a one-line summary" completed

WorkflowAgentStart.description: From the run's `journal.jsonl` (`tail?workflow=<run id>`): a `started` line. `agent_id` is what to tail with `workflow=<run id>&subagent=<agent_id>`.

label.description: The line's `label`, or `agent` when it had none.

phase.description: The line's `phase`; absent when it had none.

WorkflowAgentStop.description: From the run's `journal.jsonl`: a `result` line for that agent.

summary.description: The line's `result`: as is when it is text, else as compact JSON; truncated to 2 KB.

examples.summary: {"file":"note8.txt","summary":"Note 8 states that giraffes eat about 38 kg of leaves a day and says the note is about topic 8."}

usage.description: Token counts of the turn's last main-thread assistant line (`message.usage` in the JSONL; the `turn_duration` line that ends a turn carries none, so the runner keeps the latest one it read and clears it at each turn end). Subagent lines (`isSidechain`, or a file under `subagents/`) never count. The context the session carries into its next turn is about `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + output_tokens`; the hub compares that with the model's context window to roll the brain over (events.schema.json `brain.rollover` reason `context_full`). Absent when no assistant line in the turn had usage. New with runner-api 0.1.7.

usage_limit.description: True when the text starts with one of Claude Code's usage-limit prefixes ("You've hit your", "You've reached your", "You're out of usage credits", …; SP4).

examples.message: You've hit your session limit · resets 2:29pm (UTC)

entry.description: The line itself, truncated to 8 KB. Only for types the runner does not know and does not drop.
